title: Move evidence acquisition from browser crawl to a backend evidence service; keep recommendation client-side
context: Browser was simultaneously operator UI, recommendation client, durable evidence database and background job processor; the last two produced the recent defects (cursor/coverage divergence, divergent readiness definitions, restart losing in-memory queue, UI blanking).
evidence_at_time: Defect list at 08:52-62; prototype had proven 496-symbol acquisition, Tradier integration, cache-backed deterministic recommendation, Fidelity handoff.
alternatives: Move both evidence acquisition AND Wheelwright (recommendation) to the backend (rejected as initial approach)
Move only evidence acquisition, retain Wheelwright client-side (selected)
Use a third-party managed data platform (rejected)
rationale: Browser lifecycle is incompatible with long-lived background acquisition; server-side recommendation would destroy instant local recomputation; no platform provides the domain-specific evidence shape.
expected_consequences: Acquisition survives reloads; one authoritative evidence state; transactional SQLite; credentials server-side; multi-process local dev; snapshot payload/schema-evolution concerns.
implementation: Implemented as TS service then retired; Java evidence-service is the sole appliance (07:7-9, live acceptance Aug 3, 2026).
subsequent: Recommendation placement later declared transitional (PL-ARCH-06, 07:436-444) and superseded in direction by PRIN-ARCH-BACKEND-AUTHORITY (principles.md:60, ratified Oct 11, 2026); 60 req/min budget superseded by ≤119/60s Production pacer (07:89-90).
amendments: Recommendation-placement half: superseded in direction (principles.md:60). Rate budget: superseded (07:405). Core extraction: current.
notes: ADR outside the 07c register. Status 'Accepted' with no named acceptor; README:156 labels it 'Ratified decision'. 'Wheelwright' here means the recommendation engine (see SN0-E010). 12:3 also calls it 'the ratified decision'.

expected_consequences: Provider replacement without domain change; reuse for future portfolio/control capabilities.
implementation: Slice 1 domain layer (04:28-40).

amendments: 02 is now subordinate to options-domain-reference for lifecycle economics (02:3).
notes: Status reads 'Accepted' but no actor named; authority_class set to proposal-only because acceptance is unattributed. ID collides with 07c ADR-001 (SN0-E011).

title: First backend slice: stateless Tradier proxy that owns the credential
context: Tradier API key compiled into browser bundle; browser made authenticated provider calls.
rationale: Smallest slice that immediately removes the credential from the browser and creates the API boundary to grow behind.
expected_consequences: Identical operator experience; credential server-side; foundation for caching/scheduling/persistence.
implementation: Implemented (13 analyzes the running proxy); later retired.
subsequent: Proxy lost cache efficiencies (13 §2) → backend ResponseCache + pacer; superseded by backend-owned acquisition (14).
notes: 'Authorized scope (after review)' at 12:358 — reviewer/authorizer not named; classed Principal-accepted provisionally.

title: Backend response cache plus ~1 req/sec internal pacing behind the facade
context: Stateless proxy tripled provider calls per symbol; frontend refreshBudget reduced to 15 to avoid 429s.
evidence_at_time: Measured pass timings and call counts (13 §1, §3).
alternatives: Add in-memory TTL cache and revert budget to 40 (selected)
rationale: Rate limiting is a provider concern that belongs behind the facade; frontend should not know per-request cost.
expected_consequences: ~40 symbols/pass, no 429 in normal operation.
implementation: 14:40-42 shows ResponseCache (90s chains, 60s quotes, 5m exp) and RequestPacer (0.9 req/sec) in place.
subsequent: Pacer at 0.9 req/sec became the declared bottleneck (16a:179); Doc 40 decomposed post-completion fixed waits; replaced by single-flight ≤119/trailing-60s (07:89-90).

title: Backend-owned self-scheduling acquisition worker with conditional-HTTP polling at 30s
context: Operator had to click Scan; browser owned acquisition orchestration.
rationale: Standard HTTP, zero-cost 304 when unchanged, evidence changes in discrete generations; only one cycle in flight.
expected_consequences: Write Desk observes rather than initiates; Scan becomes optional/admin.
implementation: Implemented (07:103 30s poll; snapshot ETag/304 frozen contract).
subsequent: Became the Evidence Appliance identity (14:7).
notes: README:158 classes 14 as 'Ratified design'; header status 'Implemented (transitional architecture)' refers to the retired TS service.

D: bounded concurrency 2 streams (not recommended for this slice)

implementation: 16a records removal and coverage bar; projections not validated in doc (16a:123).
subsequent: Doc 40 shows a similar fixed-wait pattern in later pacer; concurrency question resurfaced and was flagged as drift in Doc 39.
notes: 'Authorized for immediate implementation' (16:344) — authorizer not named.

title: SQLite persistence: persist facts/derive trust, absence as resolution, generation on publication, test-oracle migration instead of runtime dual-write

Lightweight displacement with InMemoryEvidenceStore as test oracle (chosen)
rationale: Choose the lightest migration mechanism that fully retires the relevant uncertainty.
expected_consequences: Restart recovery; universe expansion to 1,286 after persistence.
implementation: Implemented in Java (07:83-84 SQLite WAL); design stack TS/better-sqlite3 historical.
subsequent: symbol_resolution persists derived state (SN0-E024).
